function.name: finance_predict_future_value
function.description: Calculate the future value of an investment given its present value, interest rate, the number of compounding periods per year, and the time horizon. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

present_value.description: The present value of the investment.

annual_interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate of the investment. This is a float type value.

compounding_periods_per_year.description: The number of times that interest is compounded per year. Default is 1 (annually).

message.content:
**Future Value Calculation**

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Present Value (\(PV\)) | \$5 000 |
| Annual Nominal Rate (\(i_{\text{yr}}\)) | 5 % |
| Compounding Frequency | Monthly (12 × per year) |
| Periodic Rate \(i_m\) | \(\dfrac{0.05}{12}=0.00416667\) |
| Number of Months \(N\) | \(3\,\text{years}\times12=\;36\) |

The future‑value formula for compound interest is  

\[
FV = PV \left(1+i_m\right)^{N}
\]

Plugging in the numbers:

\[
FV = 5\,000 \;\bigl(1+0.00416667\bigr)^{36}
   = 5\,000 \;(1.00416667)^{36}
\]

Using a quick exponentiation (or a simple spreadsheet/calculator):

\[
(1.00416667)^{36} \approx 1.1609
\]

Therefore,

\[
FV \approx 5\,000 \times 1.1609 \approx \$5,\!804.50
\]

---

### Result  
After **3 years**, investing **\$5 000** at an annual nominal rate of **5 %** compounded **monthly** will grow to approximately **\$5,805** (rounded to the nearest dollar).

Feel free to let me know if you’d like this rounded differently or want additional details on how the compounding works!
